# Manifold Untangling — invariance as a geometry problem with a fixed-complexity reader

**All images of one object, generated by all identity-preserving transformations of it, form a low-dimensional *object identity manifold* in population-response space. Recognition is separating one such manifold from all others. Early in a sensory hierarchy the manifolds are curved and interleaved ("crumpled paper"), so no hyperplane separates them; the job of the cascade is to **flatten and align** them until a single weighted sum does. No information is created — it is reformatted, and the measure of the reformatting is *how simple the downstream reader is allowed to be*.**

> **Provenance.** DiCarlo, Zoccolan & Rust 2012, *How does the brain solve visual object recognition?*, Neuron 73(3):415–434 (`raw/dicarlo-2012-brain-visual-object-recognition.md`), extending DiCarlo & Cox 2007. The biological case is [[wiki/entities/ventral-visual-stream.md]]; this page holds the transferable formulation, the success criterion, and the three proposed mechanisms — one of which (temporal-contiguity learning) is a live objective for machine systems with in-vivo causal evidence behind it.

---

## Formal statement

Let `r(I) ∈ R^N` be the population response to image `I`, and let `T` be the group (not necessarily a group — see open problems) of identity-preserving transformations. For object `o`:

```
M_o = { r(T(I_o)) : T ∈ 𝒯 }          the object identity manifold, dim(M_o) = d ≪ N
```

**Recognition** = find `w, θ` such that `sign(wᵀr − θ)` separates `M_o` from `⋃_{o' ≠ o} M_{o'}`.

| Stage | Geometry | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Retina / LGN | Point-wise spatial sensors ⇒ manifolds nearly as tangled as pixels | Linear separation impossible; identity is present but not *explicit* |
| V1 | ~30× dimensionality expansion, nonlinear ⇒ overcomplete re-representation, manifolds "spread out" | Measurably better than pixels, still far below human performance (Pinto et al. 2008a) |
| V2 → V4 → pIT | Progressive flattening and alignment | Monotone rise in linear decodability |
| IT | Flat, separated, aligned sheets | A few hundred units + one weighted sum ⇒ near-ceiling, generalizing across transformations |

**"Aligned" is the part usually dropped in retelling, and it is the part that pays.** The picture is not just unfurling two crumpled sheets but *laying them on top of each other*, so the surface coordinates of each sheet are the nuisance variables (position, scale, pose) in a common frame. That is why the same population supports both "which object?" and "where was it?" from one linear read, and why no later binding stage is needed.

---

## The success criterion, and why it is a real one

> **A representation is better if object identity is easier to decode from it *with a fixed-complexity reader*, tested on transformation conditions held out from the decoder's training.**

| Property | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **Monotone across stages** | Gives a per-layer score, so a cascade can be audited stage by stage rather than end to end |
| **Needs no encoding model** | Applies exactly where per-unit description fails ([[wiki/concepts/predictive-adequacy.md]]'s depth gradient), which is where the wiki's interests start |
| **Reader complexity is the free parameter, and fixing it is the whole method** | With an unbounded reader every stage from the retina onward scores perfectly, because information is never created. The criterion is only informative once the reader is capped |
| **Held-out *transformations*, not held-out samples** | The generalization axis is the nuisance variable — decoders trained at one position tested at another (1.5°, 3°), one scale tested at 0.33×–3×, one context tested in another |
| **Falsifiable at the single-unit level** | Predicts *tolerance* (rank-order preservation under transformation, i.e. separable shape × nuisance tuning) rather than invariance — and predicts the observed selectivity/tolerance **trade-off**, which grandmother-cell accounts get backwards |

**Relation to the wiki's other geometry instruments.** Untangling is the ancestor of cross-condition generalization performance (CCGP) in [[wiki/concepts/population-geometry.md]]: both train a linear decoder on some conditions and test on held-out ones, and both score *format* rather than presence. The difference is what is held out — CCGP holds out the values of *other task variables*, untangling holds out *transformations of the same object* — and the parallelism score is the geometric statement of exactly the alignment clause above. Neither literature cites the other; they are the same instrument discovered twice, in vision and in prefrontal cognition.

---

## Cortically local subspace untangling — the proposed mechanism

The hypothesis is a **meta job description** replicated at every cortical locus, not a transfer function:

> *Take your afferents. Apply nonlinearities and learning rules that adjust your input weights using only the activity of those afferents. You do not know what an object is. Your output representation should nonetheless be one in which object identity is more untangled than your input's.*

Held by a ~40K-neuron, ~10K-in/~10K-out, **dimensionality-preserving** block ([[wiki/entities/ventral-visual-stream.md]]), tiled laterally and stacked vertically. Each block sees a 1–10K-dimensional slice rather than the full ~1M-dimensional problem — which is what makes the local job both wirable and learnable from finite experience.

| # | Mechanism | Status | What it buys |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Architectural nonlinearity + divisive normalization** | Demonstrated: NLN-like stacks with **random, unlearned filters** already produce easier-to-decode manifolds, largely on the strength of normalization (Pinto et al. 2008b; Jarrett et al. 2009) | Flattening for free, before any data. The cheapest component and the one with no learning cost ([[wiki/concepts/inhibitory-control-of-coding.md]]) |
| 2 | **Match the dynamic range to natural input statistics** | Efficient-coding lineage (Olshausen & Field 1996; Simoncelli & Olshausen 2001); supported by higher stream levels being more tuned to *natural* feature conjunctions than lower ones (Rust & DiCarlo 2010) | Do not spend representational capacity on inputs that never occur |
| 3 | **Unsupervised temporal-contiguity learning** | Causally demonstrated in vivo — see below | **The nuisance directions themselves.** This is the mechanism that supplies invariance rather than assuming it |

---

## Mechanism 3: time as the teacher for invariance

**The claim.** Object identity is temporally stable; retinal images are not. So *directions in population-response space along which activity moves on a fast timescale are, on average, the identity-preserving directions.* An unsupervised rule that makes temporally adjacent inputs produce similar outputs therefore factorizes identity from nuisance without ever being told what an object is. Lineage: Földiák 1991; Wallis & Rolls 1997; Wiskott & Sejnowski 2002 (slow feature analysis); Stryker 1992; Fazl et al. 2009.

| Evidence | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Supply is enormous and free** | Saccade-driven image translations alone give on the order of **10⁸ position-change experiences per year of life** |
| **It is causal, not correlational** | Altering the temporal statistics of experience — swapping object identity during the saccade so that one object at position A is reliably followed by a *different* object at position B — **destroys existing position and size tolerance in IT neurons and builds new (incorrect) tolerance**, within hours (Li & DiCarlo 2008) |
| **It reaches behaviour** | The same manipulation predictably changes human object perception (Cox et al. 2005) |
| **It is unsupervised in the strong sense** | The instruction is available in the raw sensory stream; no labels, no reward, no task |
| **Shape is the residual, not the target** | Under this scheme "shape coding" is never an explicit goal — shape is *whatever natural image variation is left over* after the temporally-specified directions are factored out. This inverts the usual framing of a vision front end |

**(brainstorm) This is a transfer into the objective slot, and the wiki's self-supervised entities are the machine form of it — with one designed-in difference that is worth naming as a gap.** Modern joint-embedding methods ([[wiki/entities/barlow-twins.md]], [[wiki/entities/byol.md]], [[wiki/entities/i-jepa.md]], [[wiki/entities/dinov2.md]]) implement "make these two views agree", exactly the temporal-contiguity rule with the pairing supplied by a **hand-designed augmentation set** — crops, colour jitter, blur. The augmentation list *is* the nuisance group, chosen by the designer, fixed for the run, and identical for every unit. The biology reads the same group off the input stream's own time structure, which has three properties the augmentation version does not: it is **discovered** rather than declared, it is **local** (each locus infers the nuisance directions of its own subspace), and it is **revisable** — Li & DiCarlo rewrote it in hours by changing the statistics. Video methods ([[wiki/entities/v-jepa-2.md]]) use time for *prediction* across a gap rather than for *equivalence*, which is a different use of the same signal. Logged as gap `G95`.

**(brainstorm) The failure mode is also predicted, and is a shortcut-learning result.** If temporal adjacency is the teacher, then any environment where distinct things are reliably adjacent in time installs an invariance that is *wrong* — which is precisely what Li & DiCarlo engineered. A machine system trained on temporal contiguity inherits a corresponding attack surface: the nuisance group it learns is a property of the capture process (camera motion, editing cuts, playlist order), not of the world. [[wiki/concepts/shortcut-learning.md]]'s framing applies unchanged, and the diagnostic is the same — test on transformation conditions the training stream's time structure never paired.

---

## The AND/OR alternation, and its 2012 scorecard

The standard instantiation (Fukushima 1980; Riesenhuber & Poggio 1999; Serre et al. 2007):

```
AND-like  (selectivity):  conjunction over different features, same location   →  new tuning
OR-like   (tolerance):    pooling (e.g. MAX) over same feature, shifted/scaled RFs  →  new tolerance
repeat
```
Both operations are variants of one normalized-LN form (Kouh & Poggio 2008), so the alternation is a *parameterization* of a single canonical unit, not two mechanisms.

| Verdict at the time of writing | Detail |
|---|---|
| Performs only **slightly better than a V1-like baseline** | Pinto et al. 2011 |
| Fails to explain human performance at **≥100 ms** presentations | Competitive only under ultra-short, backward-masked viewing (Serre et al. 2007a; Pinto et al. 2010) |
| **Confusion patterns do not match IT's** | Kayaert et al. 2005; Kiani et al. 2007; Kriegeskorte et al. 2008 |
| Conclusion drawn | "These are not details of the problem — understanding them **is** the problem." The proposed method is a high-throughput screen over thousands of instantiated algorithms with unsupervised parameters learned from natural video, selected by optimized recognition tests; that procedure had already beaten hand-built state-of-the-art computer vision (Pinto et al. 2009) |

**The methodological move is the durable part**: replace *one word model per paper* with a parameterized algorithm family plus a screening criterion, and let the search select. Written in 2012, it is a recognizable description of neural architecture search — and, read against [[wiki/concepts/objective-identifiability.md]], it also names the trap: a screen selects for the criterion, so a family screened on recognition accuracy alone yields models that match accuracy and need not match the neural data at all. The review's own answer is to screen on *both*, which is the only version that carries information.

---

## Applying this to a reasoning model

| Item | How it transfers |
|---|---|
| **Per-layer, fixed-reader decodability as a training-time diagnostic** | Cheap and unused here: probe each block with a capped-complexity reader on *held-out transformation conditions*, and require the score to rise monotonically with depth. A layer where it plateaus is doing something other than untangling — including, possibly, nothing |
| **Untangling for non-perceptual variables** (brainstorm) | The manifold argument never mentions vision. Substitute "instance of a relational structure" for "object" and "surface realization" for "identity-preserving transformation" and the target of [[wiki/concepts/latent-graph-discovery.md]]'s meta-graph/instance-graph split is a manifold-alignment problem: all instantiations of one abstract structure should form a flat, aligned manifold whose surface coordinates are the instance-specific bindings. The wiki's `g`/`x` factorization and this page's "sheet aligned so its surface coordinates are the nuisance variables" are, geometrically, the same object |
| **The nuisance variables are kept, not discarded** | Invariance is achieved *at the readout* while position/scale/pose remain decodable in the same code. Any factorized architecture that throws the nuisance code away has bought invariance at the cost of the questions that need it back — and re-binding later is exactly what the biology avoids |
| **Tolerance is the right unit-level target** | Rank-order preservation over a limited range, per unit, with the population covering the range. Demanding per-unit invariance is measurably counterproductive: the most selective units are the least tolerant |
| **A local, per-block objective** | No architecture in the wiki has one. Every block here is trained only by the global loss; the untangling proposal says each block should have the *same* local objective, which would make depth a matter of stacking rather than of end-to-end credit assignment ([[wiki/concepts/biologically-plausible-credit-assignment.md]]) |

---

## Open problems

- **"Subspace untangling" has no formal definition.** The operational stand-in — identity is easier to linearly decode at the output than the input — is a *test*, not an objective; nothing yet says what to minimize. Making it differentiable is the step that would turn this page from a description into a method.
- **The transformations are not a group.** Position and scale compose and invert; pose, illumination, clutter and intraclass shape do not. Everything geometric here is stated for a manifold generated by an arbitrary indexed family, and the alignment claim (common surface coordinates across objects) is strictly weaker than it looks once "the same transformation applied to a different object" stops being well defined.
- **Dimensionality-preserving blocks and manifold flattening are in tension.** Flattening a curved `d`-manifold generally needs an expansion first (V1's 30× is exactly that), yet the proposed motif preserves dimensionality. Where the expansion budget lives across a stack of equal-width blocks is unaddressed.
- **The linear reader is asserted, not derived.** "A downstream neuron computes a weighted sum and thresholds" is the justification, but real downstream circuits are recurrent and normalizing, so the true reader class is somewhere between linear and the next stage of the same cascade. The criterion is only as principled as that bound.
- **No account of how the local objectives compose.** Every locus improving its own subspace's decodability does not obviously imply the top of the stack is optimal — the review calls this a hypothesis and does not prove it. It is the same compositionality hole [[wiki/concepts/predictive-adequacy.md]] notes for encoding models, one level up.

---

## Connections

- **[[wiki/entities/ventral-visual-stream.md]]** — the biological system this is the computational theory of: the measured monotone rise in linear decodability across V1 → V4 → IT, the ~40K-neuron block hypothesized to run the local objective, and the tolerance-not-invariance single-unit phenomenology the geometry predicts.
- **[[wiki/concepts/population-geometry.md]]** — the same instrument family arrived at from cognitive tasks: CCGP holds out *conditions of other variables* where untangling holds out *transformations of the same object*, and the parallelism score formalizes this page's "aligned sheets" clause; neither literature cites the other.
- **[[wiki/concepts/linear-representation-hypothesis.md]]** — the fixed-complexity reader is what makes untangling measurable, and this page supplies the reason the assumption is not merely convenient: capping the reader is the only way a "no information is created" cascade can be scored at all.
- **[[wiki/concepts/predictive-adequacy.md]]** — the complementary criterion, running in the opposite direction over the same tissue: per-unit predictive adequacy *falls* with depth (81% → 40% → 10% → none) while population untangling *rises*, so which of the two is used decides whether the ventral stream reads as understood or unexplained.
- **[[wiki/concepts/inhibitory-control-of-coding.md]]** — mechanism 1 of the proposal, and the strongest result in it: divisive normalization flattens manifolds measurably *with random unlearned filters*, so part of invariance is architectural and costs no data.
- **[[wiki/entities/early-visual-system.md]]** — the stage where the manifolds are still nearly as tangled as pixels, and the source of the normalization arithmetic mechanism 1 depends on; also the ~30× V1 expansion that this page's flattening argument needs and the proposed dimensionality-preserving block does not supply.
- **[[wiki/entities/barlow-twins.md]]** — the machine form of mechanism 3's objective with the pairing hand-designed: its invariance term is "make two views agree" and its decorrelation term is the factorial-code requirement, together an augmentation-defined version of the nuisance group that biology infers from time.
- **[[wiki/entities/byol.md]]** — same substitution, and the cleanest demonstration that the pairing rule is doing the work: the biological version replaces the augmentation distribution with the temporal statistics of the input stream, which is a distribution the agent could in principle observe rather than one the designer supplies.
- **[[wiki/entities/v-jepa-2.md]]** — the closest machine system to mechanism 3's data source and the furthest from its objective: it uses video time for *prediction across a gap* rather than for *equivalence between neighbours*, so the nuisance directions are never explicitly factored out.
- **[[wiki/concepts/shortcut-learning.md]]** — mechanism 3's predicted failure mode, already demonstrated in vivo: reliably pairing distinct objects across a saccade installs a *wrong* invariance in IT within hours, so any system that learns its nuisance group from temporal adjacency inherits the capture process's biases as invariances.
- **[[wiki/concepts/latent-graph-discovery.md]]** — (brainstorm) the same geometry stated for non-perceptual content: all instantiations of one meta-graph should form a flat aligned manifold whose surface coordinates are the instance bindings, which makes the `g`/`x` factorization a manifold-alignment target rather than only an architectural wish.
- **[[wiki/concepts/objective-identifiability.md]]** — prices the review's proposed method: screening a large algorithm family selects for whatever the screen measures, so a family selected on recognition accuracy alone is guaranteed to match accuracy and licensed to claim nothing about the mechanism; the two-criterion screen (behaviour *and* neural data) is the only informative version.
- **[[wiki/concepts/neuroscience-ai-transfer.md]]** — mechanism 3 is one of the very few entries that lands in that page's near-empty *objective* slot, and the only one carrying an in-vivo causal manipulation (tolerance destroyed and rebuilt by altered temporal statistics) rather than a post-hoc resemblance.
- **[[wiki/concepts/biologically-plausible-credit-assignment.md]]** — what a per-block local objective would buy: if every block runs the same unsupervised untangling rule, depth is added by stacking rather than by propagating a global error, which is the architectural payoff the local-learning literature keeps looking for.
- **[[wiki/entities/dinov2.md]]** — the joint-embedding model whose frozen-feature protocol this page tightens: capping the reader is half of the discipline, and DINOv2 supplies that half while splitting on held-out *samples* rather than held-out transformations.
- **[[wiki/entities/i-jepa.md]]** — what a joint-embedding objective buys, stated in vision-neuroscience terms: flat, separated, aligned object manifolds — and the reason this model's probes under-report, since they hold out samples rather than position shifts, 0.33×–3× scale and changed context.
